accommodation.description: URJC offers student residences across its campuses in Móstoles and Fuenlabrada. The Erasmus Student Network (ESN Madrid) runs a housing group. Budget for a shared flat is €400–700/month.
tips: Apply to URJC housing in June — spots fill very quickly.
Look for rooms near Móstoles or Fuenlabrada campus to save on transport.
Many landlords require a guarantor (aval) — ask URJC international office for alternatives.
Join the GLOBE & Erasmus WhatsApp groups; students often share flats.
Ask for a rental contract (contrato de arrendamiento) — you will need it for your TIE application.

transport.description: Madrid has one of Europe's best metro networks. Campuses in Móstoles and Fuenlabrada are served by Cercanías commuter trains from Atocha station.
options: EMT city buses — same Metrobús card valid
Cercanías (commuter train) — Zones A–B for campus
Renfe long-distance trains — for weekend travel around Spain
Lime/Bolt scooters — available in central Madrid
tips: Get an Abono Joven (under 26): unlimited Metro+Bus+Cercanías for €20/month.
Top up your transport card at any metro station machine.
Download the METRO MADRID and CERCANÍAS apps for real-time maps.
Taxi apps: Cabify and FREE NOW are safer than street taxis.

simCards.recommended: Digi Mobile — 50GB for ~€7/month (best value for students)
tips: You need your NIE number to sign a phone contract. Use a prepaid SIM until you have your NIE.
Digi and Lebara are the best budget options.
Make sure your phone is unlocked before arriving.

residencePermit.name: TIE — Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero
residencePermit.timeline: Apply within 30 days of arrival at the Oficina de Extranjería
documents: Valid passport + photocopy of all pages
University enrollment certificate (Carta de Admisión from URJC)
Proof of accommodation (rental contract or residence letter)
Proof of financial means (Erasmus grant letter or bank statements)
residencePermit.notes: EU citizens: register at the Registro Central de Extranjeros instead (much simpler). Non-EU students must arrive on a long-stay visa obtained from the Spanish embassy BEFORE travelling.

healthInsurance: EU citizens: bring your European Health Insurance Card (EHIC/CEAM). Non-EU students: private insurance is mandatory. Recommended: Mapfre Estudiantes (~€40/month), Adeslas, Sanitas. Policy must cover €30,000+ and repatriation.
banking: Revolut, N26, or Wise work perfectly for receiving Erasmus grants (SEPA transfers). If you want a Spanish account: Openbank (Santander's online bank, no fees) is easiest. Avoid traditional banks with maintenance fees.
additionalNotes: The Erasmus grant is paid monthly to your European bank account. Confirm details with URJC before arrival.
URJC has campuses in Móstoles, Fuenlabrada, Alcorcón, and Vicálvaro — confirm which campus your courses are on.

accommodation.description: Bangor University offers on-campus halls of residence — apply immediately upon receiving your acceptance letter, as places are very competitive. Bangor town has private rental options within walking distance of campus.
tips: Apply for university halls the same day you receive your acceptance.
Bangor is a small, walkable city — living near the high street means easy access to campus.
Private rentals often require a UK guarantor — international students may need to pay several months upfront.
Check if your halls include utilities (gas, electricity, internet) in the price.

transport.description: Bangor is small and walkable. For wider travel, bus and train services connect to the rest of Wales and the UK.
options: Walking/cycling — most of Bangor accessible on foot
Sherpa'r Wyddfa buses — local Gwynedd bus network
Arriva Trains Wales — Bangor station on the North Wales mainline
National Rail — discounted with 16-25 Railcard (£30/year, saves 1/3)
FlixBus / National Express — budget coaches to Manchester, London
tips: Buy a 16-25 Railcard immediately — it pays for itself in one trip.
Cardiff is ~3.5 hours by train; Liverpool and Manchester ~1.5 hours.
Snowdonia National Park is on Bangor's doorstep — hire bikes for weekends.

simCards.recommended: Three UK — includes free data roaming in 71 countries including all EU states
tips: All SIM providers require only a passport — no local address needed.
GiffGaff: no contract, pay monthly, good EU roaming.
Smarty (owned by Three) has the cheapest plans — from £5/month.

residencePermit.name: Student Visa (UK) + BRP (Biometric Residence Permit)
residencePermit.timeline: Apply for Student Visa 6–8 weeks before travel. Collect BRP within 10 days of arrival.
documents: Valid passport (6+ months beyond course end)
CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) from Bangor University
Online UK visa application at gov.uk
Biometric enrolment at UK Visa Application Centre
TB test certificate if from a listed country
residencePermit.notes: Post-Brexit, EU/EEA citizens need a UK Student Visa like all other international students for courses over 6 months. For courses of 6 months or under, a Standard Visitor Visa (£115) may suffice — confirm with Bangor University.

healthInsurance: Students who pay the IHS surcharge with their visa get full NHS access. Register with a GP in Bangor immediately after arrival. NHS is free at point of use once registered.
banking: Monzo or Starling are easiest — open online, no UK address needed initially. HSBC has an international student account you can open before travelling. Use Revolut or Wise for daily spending to avoid foreign transaction fees.
additionalNotes: The UK uses £GBP — not Euros. £1 ≈ €1.17 (check current rate).
Wales has its own language (Welsh/Cymraeg) — signs are bilingual.
Emergency number in the UK: 999. Non-emergency police: 101.

duration: Third Semester — Summer School, University of Tlaxcala

accommodation.description: UATx offers limited student housing. Most GLOBE students rent private rooms in Tlaxcala city, which is very affordable. Sharing is common.
tips: Contact UATx international relations well in advance — they often coordinate shared housing.
Tlaxcala city centre is safe and walkable.
Airbnb is a good option for the first week while you find permanent accommodation.

transport.description: Tlaxcala uses a combi (minibus) network that covers the city cheaply. Buses connect regularly to Puebla and Mexico City.
options: CAPU terminal (Puebla) — connections to Mexico City
Uber and InDriver — available in Tlaxcala city
tips: Always use Uber or InDriver rather than flagging taxis — safer and transparent pricing.
Mexico City is ~2 hours from Tlaxcala by direct bus — great for weekends.
Download the InDriver app — often cheaper than Uber in smaller cities.

simCards.recommended: Telcel — best nationwide coverage, essential for travel outside Tlaxcala
tips: Buy a Telcel SIM at any OXXO store — just bring your passport.
Telcel plans: ~MXN 200/month for 4GB + unlimited WhatsApp.
Signal in Tlaxcala city is excellent.

residencePermit.name: FMM Tourist Entry Card (Forma Migratoria Múltiple)
residencePermit.timeline: Issued on arrival at Mexican port of entry — valid up to 180 days
documents: FMM form (available on the plane or at the border)
residencePermit.notes: The 6-week summer school is well within Mexico's 180-day tourist entry allowance. Keep your FMM card safe — you must surrender it when you exit Mexico. Check your nationality in the Visa Checker as some nationalities require a visitor visa.

healthInsurance: Travel health insurance is strongly recommended covering medical evacuation. Consider WorldNomads or AXA Travel for the summer school period.
banking: Notify your home bank of travel to Mexico to avoid your card being blocked. Wise and Revolut cards work well. Withdraw cash from major ATMs: BBVA, Banamex, HSBC México. Small vendors may only accept cash (MXN).
additionalNotes: Tlaxcala is consistently ranked one of Mexico's safest states.
Register with your home country's embassy upon arrival.
Water: drink only bottled or filtered water.

accommodation.description: University housing should be applied for in spring before departure. Private rentals are available via Uniplaces and Idealista PT, but prices have risen significantly in Lisbon and Porto.
tips: Apply for university housing in spring (April/May) — places are limited.
Lisbon and Porto are expensive — consider suburbs with metro/train access.
Always get a written rental contract — you will need it for your NIF and AR application.

transport.description: Portugal has good public transport in urban areas. Lisbon has an excellent metro; Porto has the Metro do Porto light rail.
options: Metro Lisboa / Metro do Porto — student monthly pass available
CP trains — intercity rail across Portugal
tips: Get a Viva Viagem card (Lisbon) or Andante card (Porto).
Apply for a Cartão Jovem (18–30 youth card, ~€6) for rail discounts.
Uber and Bolt work well in all major Portuguese cities.

simCards.recommended: MEO — best rural and nationwide coverage
tips: MEO and NOS both offer good student plans ~€15/month for 20GB+.
You do not need a NIF to buy a prepaid SIM.
Portugal has strong 4G coverage; 5G in major cities.

residencePermit.name: Autorização de Residência para Estudo (AR) — preceded by Type D Study Visa
residencePermit.timeline: Obtain Type D visa before departure; register with AIMA within 4 months of arrival
documents: Type D Study Visa (from Portuguese embassy — non-EU only)
NIF (Portuguese tax number — get in first week)
residencePermit.notes: EU citizens: No visa needed. Register at the Câmara Municipal within 90 days. Non-EU: Apply for Type D Study Visa before travelling. After arrival, register with AIMA within 4 months. Get your NIF first — required for renting and banking.

healthInsurance: EU citizens: EHIC/CEAM card gives access to public healthcare (SNS). Register with a local Centro de Saúde. Non-EU students: private health insurance required for visa.
banking: Get your NIF first — required to open any bank account in Portugal. Banking options: Millennium BCP, Caixa Geral, ActivoBank (no-fee). MB WAY is Portugal's universal mobile payment system.
additionalNotes: Partner university and city for Semester 4 will be confirmed by the coordination office.
The NIF (Número de Identificação Fiscal) is your Portuguese tax number — get it in your first week.
Portugal is part of the Schengen Area.
